prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP’s 2015 manifesto sets out a sovereigntist, pro-democracy, pro-Britain programme: leave the EU, take back control of laws, borders and money, and redirect wasted spending to frontline priorities without raising taxes or debt.

Core fiscal approach and savings
- Leave the EU, save £9bn net annually; cut foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI; scrap HS2; replace the unfair Barnett Formula with a needs-based system; end health tourism; and cut the cost of Westminster (fewer MPs/ministers, abolish unnecessary departments and quangos, clamp down on “fake charities”). Cebr assessed these plans as sound.
- Use savings to invest: +£12bn for the NHS; +£5.2bn for social care; +£1.5bn for mental health and dementia; 6,000 extra police/prison/border staff; defence to at least 2% of GDP; support carers (+£572/yr); stamp duty relief for new brownfield homes.

Taxes and economy
- Raise the personal allowance to at least £13,000; take the minimum wage out of income tax; raise the 40% threshold to £55,000 with a new 30% band; abolish inheritance tax; increase marriage/civil partner transfer; long-term aim for a flatter 20/30/40 system.
- Restore UK tax sovereignty to stop multinationals shifting profits; allow VAT zero-rating (e.g., sanitary products, listed-building repairs).
- Cut business rates for small firms with a new 20% relief up to £50,000 rateable value; tackle late payments by big companies; improve SME access to finance.

Immigration and borders
- Immigration is about space, not race. End EU free movement by leaving the EU; introduce an Australian-style points system; 5-year moratorium on unskilled immigration; 50,000 cap on skilled work visas; equal, non-discriminatory visa regime.
- Five-year qualification for benefits and non-urgent NHS access; no amnesty for illegal immigrants; fast deportation of foreign criminals; revoke citizenship obtained by fraud; treat joining terror groups as forfeiting citizenship (with legal changes).

NHS and social care
- NHS free at point of need, but not an “International Health Service.” End health tourism via insurance/eligibility rules.
- Recruit 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives; GP pilots in A&E; free hospital parking; stronger mental health and perinatal services; major dementia investment; scrap PFI use; replace CQC/Monitor with elected county health boards; “licence to manage” for NHS managers; scrap damaging EU directives (e.g., Working Time) and exclude the NHS from TTIP.
- Restore social care funding to 2010 levels; integrate health and social care under the NHS; dignity code; fair deal for home-care workers.

Education, skills, families
- More school choice: support grammars, vocational/technical routes, SEN schools; abolish SATs at 7; cut teacher workload; first-aid in PSHE; Ofsted focused on teaching quality; free STEMM tuition for UK students who work in-discipline in Britain for five years; limit low-value degree expansion.
- Childcare: deregulate to expand places and cut costs; wraparound care 8am–6pm at primaries; emergency childcare registers.
- Presumption of 50–50 shared parenting; war widows’ pensions for life; flexible state-pension window.

Housing and environment
- Build on brownfield first: national register, remediation grants, stamp duty relief; bring empties back into use; local homes for local people; restrict RTB/Help to Buy to British citizens (with Armed Forces exception); protect the green belt and prime farmland; genuine localism via referendums.

Energy and transport
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; scrap green levies/ETS to cut bills; back shale with safeguards and a Sovereign Wealth Fund; support coal, nuclear and hydro; end subsidies for onshore wind/large solar.
- Scrap HS2; oppose road-pricing tech; end DCPC; fair HGV levy for foreign trucks; protect classic cars.

Law, order, justice and defence
- 3,500 more frontline police/prison staff and +2,500 Border Agency staff; leave ECHR and adopt a British Bill of Rights; end the European Arrest Warrant; decriminalise TV licence non-payment; curb FOBT stakes to £2.
- Rebuild Armed Forces, keep Trident, accelerate carrier capability, strengthen intelligence with a single Director.

Farming, fishing, heritage, culture, trade
- Replace CAP with a fair UK Single Farm Payment focused on family farms; tough animal welfare (ban live exports, CCTV in abattoirs).
- Leave the CFP; restore a 200-mile UK EEZ; prioritise under-10m boats; end destructive methods.
- Zero VAT on listed-building repairs; save pubs (smoking rooms by choice, targeted beer tax relief).
- Promote British values, free speech and integration; English (plus Welsh/Gaelic) for official documents; St George’s and St David’s Days as bank holidays.
- Brexit roadmap: swift EU exit under Article 50, UK–EU free-trade deal, reclaim WTO seat, expand global trade.
